---

### 📊 Summary Comparison Table (2023)

| Metric / Dimension | **Nalanda** (2023) | **Purnia** (2023) | **Gap (Nalanda − Purnia)** |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Enrolled Women** ($E$) | $1,450$ | $1,200$ | $+250\text{ trainees}$ |
| **Completed Training** ($C$) | $1,276$ | $972$ | $+304\text{ graduates}$ |
| **Employed at 6 Months** ($M$) | $1,046$ | $719$ | $+327\text{ employed}$ |
| **Formula 1: Completion Rate (%)** | **$\mathbf{88.0\%}$** | **$\mathbf{81.0\%}$** | **$\mathbf{+7.0\text{ pp}}$** |
| **Formula 2: 6-Month Employment Rate (%)** | **$\mathbf{82.0\%}$** | **$\mathbf{74.0\%}$** | **$\mathbf{+8.0\text{ pp}}$** |
| *Overall Placement Yield ($\frac{M}{E}\times 100$)* | $72.1\%$ | $59.9\%$ | $+12.2\text{ pp}$ |
| *Average Monthly Wage* | ₹$11,400$ | ₹$10,100$ | $+₹1,300$ |

---

### 📐 Step-by-Step Calculations & Both Percentage Point Gaps

#### 1. Formula 1: Training Completion Rate Gap
$$\text{Completion Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Women Completed Training}}{\text{Total Women Enrolled}} \right) \times 100$$

* **Nalanda:** $\frac{1,276}{1,450} \times 100 = \mathbf{88.0\%}$
* **Purnia:** $\frac{972}{1,200} \times 100 = \mathbf{81.0\%}$

$$\text{Gap}_{\text{Completion}} = 88.0\% - 81.0\% = \mathbf{+7.0\text{ percentage points (pp)}}$$
> **Gap 1 Result:** Nalanda leads Purnia in training completion rate by **$7.0\text{ percentage points}$**.

---

#### 2. Formula 2: 6-Month Post-Training Employment Rate Gap
$$\text{6-Month Employment Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Graduates Employed at 6 Months}}{\text{Women Completed Training}} \right) \times 100$$

* **Nalanda:** $\frac{1,046}{1,276} \times 100 = \mathbf{82.0\%}$ ($81.97\%$)
* **Purnia:** $\frac{719}{972} \times 100 = \mathbf{74.0\%}$ ($73.97\%$)

$$\text{Gap}_{\text{Employment}} = 82.0\% - 74.0\% = \mathbf{+8.0\text{ percentage points (pp)}}$$
> **Gap 2 Result:** Nalanda leads Purnia in 6-month employment outcome by **$8.0\text{ percentage points}$**.

---
